question:
A 30-year-old female runner with a history of plantar fasciitis presents to the clinic complaining of right
foot pain that started one week ago after she began marathon training. She recalls the pain began
following a misstep during a stride. She describes the pain as a 7/10 achy sensation that worsens with
movement of the right foot. On examination, there is moderate diffuse swelling around the right ankle,
and the pain increases with passive abduction, dorsiflexion, and eversion of the foot. What is the most
likely diagnosis? Answer Choices: (A) Pronation ankle sprain (B) Posterior fibular head somatic
dysfunction (C) Anterior talofibular ligament tear (D) Syndesmotic ankle sprain (E) Anterior fibular head

somatic dysfunction (F) Tibialis posterior tendinopathy (G) Deltoid ligament strain (H) Supination ankle
sprain (I) Peroneal tendon subluxation (J) Calcaneal stress fracture
 A. Calcaneal stress fracture
B. Syndesmotic ankle sprain
C. Supination ankle sprain
D. Anterior talofibular ligament tear
E. Peroneal tendon subluxation
F. Posterior fibular head somatic dysfunction
G. Pronation ankle sprain
H. Anterior fibular head somatic dysfunction
I. Deltoid ligament strain
J. Tibialis posterior tendinopathy
